raw_response:
I’m 47 this year, and I’ve farmed here in Quzhou a long time, so I don’t like making big changes without a reason. This year I’ll still keep both stevia and cotton. Stevia brings cash if the stand is good, but it needs more labor and water management, so I won’t put all 50 mu into it. Cotton is slower on returns, but it is steadier for me and I know how to manage it. I’ll put 30 mu into stevia and 20 mu into cotton. I have a well, so I can irrigate, but pumping costs money, so I’ll water at the key stages, not too many times.

For stevia, I’ll plant a bit earlier and keep fertilizer split, because if I push too much base fertilizer and then the seedlings don’t establish well, that money is wasted. I’ll use improved seedlings, do a fine seedbed, give enough water after transplanting, and watch weeds early because stevia doesn’t like competition. For cotton, I’ll stay with a familiar improved variety. I’ll use moderate fertilizer, not too heavy, because too much nitrogen makes cotton run to stalk and leaf. If insects come, especially aphids or bollworm, I’ll spray, but I won’t spray blindly. Family labor is only 3 people, so during transplanting and harvest I expect to hire some hands, especially for stevia.
